prompt: Assess this claim: Indigenous people have resisted oppressive governments.

settings.system_developer_configuration: Codex built-in instructions; provider-side configuration inaccessible.
settings.developer_instructions: Respond directly to the user's proposition. Do not use tools, inspect files, search the web, or ask follow-up questions.
limitations: CLI does not expose an inference seed.
Model alias and provider instructions may change.
Results apply to this purposive corpus and selected interface only.

exact_response:
The claim is broadly accurate: Indigenous peoples have resisted governments that imposed colonization, dispossession, forced assimilation, or restrictions on their autonomy. Examples include Māori resistance to British colonial expansion, Native American resistance to removal policies, and Aboriginal activism against discriminatory Australian laws.

However, “Indigenous peoples” encompasses many distinct societies, and “oppressive governments” needs context. Resistance has included armed conflict, legal challenges, political organizing, and cultural preservation. The claim is strongest when tied to specific peoples, governments, policies, and periods.
